summary: Enabled independent EPLB state for speculative draft runners. Draft model construction and execution now use draft-local expert-location metadata, distribution recording, dynamic rebalancing, and an independently padded redundant-expert count. For the reported DeepSeek case, a 256-expert draft is padded to 288 physical slots at EP size 72 or 144 without changing the already aligned 288-expert target.

tests.what_was_measured: 97 runtime-context tests and 140 subtests, including target/draft EPLB isolation, exception-safe restoration, explicit-redundancy compatibility, and 256/288-expert alignment at EP 72/144.
35 existing EPLB algorithm and no-A2A regression tests.
On one AMD Instinct MI350X, 4096 routes through a 256-logical/288-physical draft mapping, including duplicate physical slots, exactly matched an independent NumPy reference.
All applicable repository formatting, lint, syntax, security, and policy hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X executed exact GPU gathers for 4096 routes across the padded draft mapping; output matched an independent NumPy reference bit-for-bit. Raw details are in reports/j-1dc6202a21d1/test-output.txt.

remaining_limitations: Only one GPU was allocated, so the requested 72- and 144-rank distributed DeepSeek/MTP serving configurations and cross-rank EPLB migrations were not executable.
DeepSeek target and MTP model weights were unavailable, so end-to-end model semantic accuracy was not measured.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture is dense and cannot validate MoE EPLB, MTP architecture behavior, or distributed execution; it was intentionally not presented as evidence.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
